title: China's solar expansion policy reduces bird diversity.
data_url: https://zenodo.org/records/22168817 (third-party replication package, MIT licence; the authors' own eight .dta files are distributed only with the Science article and are NOT in any open repository)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the only public package that touches this analysis (Zenodo 22168817, 995 KB zip, MIT licence) and opened both Stata files with pandas: ebird_county_month.dta = 12,996 rows x 17 columns, 1,303 Chinese counties, 2014-2023, zero missing values, zero duplicate (county, year, month) keys; gbif_county_month.dta = 39,873 rows x 7 columns, 1,531 counties, three source groups (all_GBIF 17,488; eBird_EOD 15,435; other_GBIF 6,950), zero missing, zero duplicate keys. Also read the 591 KB critique PDF (Zenodo 22277127) which lists every variable, its unit and its summary statistics (N = 46,528). Confirmed the package's own README and fetch_zhang_data.py state the eight source files are NOT redistributed, and tried science.org twice (article page and suppl_file URL): HTTP 403 both times. Zenodo, Dryad and Harvard Dataverse searches returned no deposit by Zhang et al.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the paper's own analysis file set: the 2,344-county coverage, the Shannon bird-diversity outcome from the China Birdwatching Record Centre, the land-cover, climate, population, carbon and photovoltaic-capacity covariates, and the 2.10% diversity reduction per one-standard-deviation increase in policy intensity. I never opened Bird.dta, PI.dta, IC.dta, Climate.dta, PD.dta, air.dta, TD.dta or BTN.dta; their contents are known to me only through the critics' documentation of them.

a1_downloadable.note: The eight Stata files that hold the label and nearly all features are distributed only with the Science article. science.org returned HTTP 403 to both the article page and the supplementary-file URL, no deposit exists on Zenodo, Dryad, Harvard Dataverse or Science Data Bank, and the one public replication package states plainly 'this repository does not redistribute them' with the fallback 'contact the corresponding author'. That is an access barrier, so A1 fails.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: ShannonBD (a bird-diversity index) is documented as a ready-made column in Bird.dta, and I saw the equivalent column ShannonBD_EBD in the eBird file I did open. Pass on documentation, not on the authors' own file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Climate, land-cover shares, population density, carbon emissions and photovoltaic capacity are all documented as plain numeric columns keyed on county and year. Not verified in the authors' files, which I could not obtain.

a4_units_stated.note: The critics' Table S2 reproduces the variable definitions with units: square kilometres for solar-farm area, degrees Celsius for temperature, metres per second for wind, log-transformed counts elsewhere, Shannon index unitless.

a5_enough_rows.note: 46,528 complete county-month rows after merging, per the critics' re-run; well above the 1,500 threshold. But the real independent unit is the county (about 2,344), and only 4,410 county-years carry genuine policy data.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The whole analysis is a few megabytes of tabular data; the critics' Stata pipeline runs in about one minute. No memory concern at all.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: I could not reconcile them and neither could the published critics: 48,900 raw bird rows, 46,528 complete rows, 46,371 in the regression, 2,344 counties claimed, 775 counties with no policy match. Worse, 54.6% of solar-farm-area values and 43.9% of policy-index values are missing and silently recoded to zero, which a published comment says reverses the headline result.

a8_label_provenance.note: The Shannon bird-diversity label is computed from the same citizen-science birdwatching records that generate three of the model's own features (number of birdwatchers, birdwatching duration, duration per person). More checklists mechanically yield more species, so the label is partly computed from the features. The published critique shows the headline association disappears once birdwatching activity is controlled for.

existing_models.name: eBird Status and Trends (Cornell Lab of Ornithology; AdaSTEM, an adaptive spatiotemporal ensemble of boosted regression trees)
existing_models.score_and_split: Covers 2,980 bird species worldwide at weekly resolution with published per-species validation metrics; data products and the ebirdst R package are openly distributed. Exact numbers not retrieved by me, only the fact that validation metrics are published alongside each species.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Correcting for the bias in where, when and how hard community scientists look for birds is named repeatedly as the central open difficulty.

existing_models.name: SatBird (a 2023 benchmark dataset and baseline models for predicting bird species encounter rates from satellite imagery plus eBird checklists)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published at the NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track with open data and code; I did not retrieve the specific metric values.

existing_models.name: Interpretable machine-learning studies of Chinese bird richness versus land use (several 2025 papers, e.g. national-scale avian species richness from human and natural factors, and urban land-use studies in Harbin and Hangzhou)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published in ecology and environmental-management journals; code and data availability not checked by me.

existing_models.name: Li and Wang (2026) re-analysis of this exact paper (ordinary least squares with county and year-month fixed effects, not machine learning)
existing_models.score_and_split: Full Stata replication package on Zenodo under an MIT licence, which I downloaded and inspected; reports that the solar-policy coefficient attenuates from -0.0125 to -0.0027 and loses significance once zero-filled county-years are dropped.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Whether any real ecological effect of solar build-out on birds exists once birdwatcher access and missing data are handled honestly.

backbone.name: None that fits. The data is a 16-column county-month economic panel; no protein, molecule, DNA or single-cell backbone applies. A remote-sensing foundation model (Prithvi or Clay) would fit satellite imagery, but that imagery is not in this dataset and would have to be assembled separately.
backbone.hardware: CPU only would suffice for the tabular data, but there is nothing to freeze; adding satellite imagery would require a GPU.
backbone.licence: The third-party replication package is MIT. The licence on the authors' own files is unknown because I could not obtain them.

integration.partner_dataset: eBird Basic Dataset and the Global Biodiversity Information Facility occurrence archive, both already processed into county-month panels inside the replication package I opened.
integration.join_key: Chinese county administrative code plus year and month; 1,275 counties overlap between the eBird and GBIF panels.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a bird-diversity signal measured by one citizen-science platform survive when the same counties and months are measured by a different platform with different observers? The critics have already answered this and found it does not.

controls.positive_control: Seasonality: any working model of monthly bird diversity in China must recover the spring and autumn migration peaks. Available in the files I opened.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the diversity label within county and confirm the solar-policy signal collapses; also fit the model on birdwatching effort alone, which the critique suggests would capture most of the apparent effect.
controls.external_validation: The eBird and GBIF county-month panels in the replication package are genuine independent measurements of the same quantity in the same counties, and the critics report no solar-policy association in either.

honest_claim_h3: A model built on this data could only claim to predict how diverse the birds recorded by Chinese volunteer birdwatchers appear to be in a given county and month, among counties where volunteers chose to go birdwatching at all, with the diversity index partly determined by how many volunteers went and for how long.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use county land cover, climate and solar-farm build-out to predict monthly bird diversity across Chinese counties.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per Chinese county per month, holding land-cover shares (farmland, grassland, forest, water), temperature, wind, population density, carbon emissions, solar-policy intensity and solar-farm area, plus birdwatching effort. The paper's merged table has 46,528 such rows (a number I read in the critics' re-run, not in the authors' files).
plain_idea.predict: The Shannon diversity index of birds for that county-month, computed from species proportions in volunteer birdwatching checklists submitted to the China Birdwatching Record Centre.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Energy-siting regulators would want to know which counties lose the most bird diversity per megawatt of solar installed; even a failed model would quantify how much of recorded diversity is really just how hard people looked.

more_or_better_data.why: eBird Status and Trends models 2,980 species worldwide from hundreds of millions of checklists at weekly resolution; this is 46,528 county-months of one aggregated index from one country. The China Birdwatching Record Centre coverage is a genuine niche, but the critics show eBird and GBIF already cover 1,275 of the same counties.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate measurements of a county-month's true diversity, so the noise floor cannot be estimated from within the data. The cross-platform comparison with eBird and GBIF gives disagreement, not calibrated uncertainty, and eBird Status and Trends already publishes per-species validation metrics.

models_beatable.why: eBird Status and Trends is a continuously maintained ensemble with published validation and an explicit effort-correction design; SatBird is a 2023 open benchmark. Neither is an old, weakly evaluated target.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Several conditions fail at once: the existing models are trained on a different platform's raw checklists rather than this county-month index, the evaluation split would differ, and I cannot even obtain the label file to run the comparison.

ml_idea: The project considered was a tabular regression predicting county-month Shannon bird diversity from land cover, climate, population and solar-farm build-out, with a held-out-county split, framed as the transfer question 'does a diversity model fitted to one citizen-science platform transfer to another?' using the eBird and GBIF panels as external validation. It dies on access to the label file and on the fact that the label is partly a function of three of the features.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from files I actually loaded: the two Stata panels together are 2.9 MB and read into pandas instantly; a gradient-boosted tree on 46,528 rows and 16 columns would cross-validate in a couple of minutes on a laptop CPU. No embeddings because no backbone applies.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether the eight authors' .dta files can be downloaded without a Science subscription. I could not get them in two attempts and the public replication package refuses to redistribute them, so this check already failed.

verdict_reason: Three Part A killers fail. A1: the label and nearly all features live in eight Stata files distributed only with the Science article (HTTP 403 for me, no repository deposit, and the one public replication package explicitly does not redistribute them, offering only 'contact the corresponding author'). A8: the Shannon diversity label is computed from the same volunteer birdwatching records that produce three of the model's features (number of observers, time spent, time per observer), so the label is partly computed from the features; a published comment shows the headline effect vanishes once observation effort is controlled. A7: the counts do not reconcile, and over half of solar-farm-area values and 44% of policy-index values are missing and silently recoded to zero. Separately, no pretrained backbone fits a 16-column county-month panel, and the task of predicting bird diversity from environment is already served at far larger scale by eBird Status and Trends and the SatBird benchmark. The downloadable part (the critics' MIT-licensed eBird and GBIF county-month panels, which I did open and which are clean) is useful evidence but contains no environmental or solar features of its own.
